hero.title: Interfaces, defects, and transport across electronic devices.
hero.description: I study how microscopic interfaces and electronic or ionic transport govern device operation, variability, and reliability. Three research pillars connect physical questions to memory devices and thin-film electronic platforms.

expertise.title: Research expertise & methods
expertise.intro: These capabilities are evidenced by first-author and collaborative studies. A listed method does not imply sole responsibility for every instrument or experiment.

areas.title: Materials & Interface Engineering
areas.method: Molecular contacts, SAMs, ALD-related thin films, and hybrid-device interfaces.
areas.question: How does local chemistry change energy alignment and trap populations?
areas.relevance: Charge injection, transport, and stable device operation.

areas.title: Electrical characterization
areas.method: Current–voltage and pulse-response studies, retention and endurance testing, and variability measurements.
areas.question: How do electronic states form, change, and persist?
areas.relevance: Quantified switching behavior and device-to-device comparison.

areas.title: Device physics & reliability
areas.method: Trap and ionic-transport analysis, analog-state readout, noise, and leakage measurements in published and ongoing work.
areas.question: Which mechanisms constrain precision and stability?
areas.relevance: Interpreting memory-state and capacitor behavior beyond a single performance number.

areas.title: Processing & Applied Devices
areas.method: Thin-film electrode studies and doctor-blade-printed interconnects in academic and collaborative programs.
areas.question: How does process-induced geometry vary between nominally identical devices?
areas.relevance: Separating initial electrical nonuniformity from changes during mechanical cycling.

contributions.heading: Molecular interfaces for reliable analog memory
contributions.question: Can hydrogen bonding at a polymer–perovskite interface improve the symmetry and stability of analog switching?
contributions.mechanism: Interfacial hydrogen bonding suppresses trap-mediated disruption of ionic and electronic response.
contributions.approach: Compare interface-controlled synaptic devices through switching and state-retention measurements.
contributions.evidence: More than eightfold lower interfacial trap density and 50 analog conductance states retained beyond 10⁴ s.
contributions.significance: Interfacial chemistry offers a physical route to more reproducible analog memory states.

contributions.heading: Defect-controlled optoelectronic memory
contributions.question: Can an intermediate layer lower trap density while preserving low-power optoelectronic switching?
contributions.mechanism: An ALD TiO₂ intermediate layer changes the device interface and reduces trapping.
contributions.approach: Relate intermediate-layer design to trap-density estimates and switching measurements.
contributions.evidence: A fifteenfold reduction in interfacial trap density, +0.24 V SET operation, and approximately 0.7 μW switching power.
contributions.significance: The study connects a controlled interface to both the switching mechanism and its operating cost.

contributions.heading: Persistent analog states conditioned by optical helicity
contributions.question: Can optical helicity condition distinguishable electronic memory states that remain readable over time?
contributions.mechanism: Helicity-dependent excitation biases persistent conductance states in a chiral perovskite synapse.
contributions.approach: Evaluate retained conductance, readout-noise-limited state capacity, and a small device array.
contributions.myContribution: Conceptualization, methodology, investigation, data curation, and original-draft writing, as listed in the publisher’s CRediT statement.
contributions.evidence: 72 experimentally distinguishable states, 10⁶ s retention, read-noise analysis, and evaluation of a 7×7 device array.
contributions.significance: The result tests whether an optical input can become a persistent analog state with measurable precision and array-level behavior.

directions.title: Interface-controlled ionic memory
directions.text: The ongoing independent project asks how interfaces, defect landscapes, and ionic motion limit multilevel precision. State-formation dynamics and low-frequency noise are being studied; specific results are still in development.

directions.title: Oxide electronics & memory reliability
directions.text: Prior ALD electrode and capacitor studies provide a basis for new questions about oxide interfaces, defect-mediated transport, dielectric behavior, and memory reliability. Experimental work in memory-specific oxide platforms is a future direction.

directions.title: Toward integrated electronic systems
directions.text: I aim to connect interface design, electrical characterization, and reliability physics to low-temperature and integrated device platforms. These system-level aims remain prospective.
